designNarrative: This diff adds CheckSlices, a cross-order fitness function that groups parsed intake Documents by slice.of and verifies digest agreement, manifest file integrity, depends-on cycles/dangling edges, and exactly-once criterion-level coverage, all behind a single FileReader seam that only cmd/loom/cmd/intake.go implements with a real os.ReadFile rooted at the project root. internal/intake stays free of os/io/fs imports, Slice is a plain YAML-tagged data struct on Order, and every cross-order rule lives as small free functions in slice_check.go matching the package's existing idiom (Check is already a free function). The CLI folds slice violations into the same invalid counter that already decides runIntakeCheck's exit code, so the 0-only-when-valid contract is extended rather than duplicated.
securitySurface: slice.spec, slice.manifest, and every manifest-listed file path are checked by isWithinProjectRoot (a lexical, pre-read guard) before readRooted ever calls FileReader — an escaping path is refused, never opened. Verified by TestReadRootedRefusesAnEscapingPathWithoutCallingRead, TestReadSpecPackageRefusesAnEscapingPath, and the 'leaves the project root' cases in TestCheckSlicesReportsEachViolationKind.
performanceSurface: CheckSlices performs zero FileReader calls when no order in the batch sets a slice block (verified independently: TestCheckSlicesReadsNothingWhenNoOrderSetsSlice passes, matching the NFR 'a directory with no slice blocks reads no extra files').
Manifest and spec reads are cached per distinct path within a slice.of group (loadGroupManifests/loadGroupSpecPackage), so N slices sharing one manifest/spec trigger one read each, not N.
testDesignReview: TestParseLeavesSliceNilWhenAbsent / TestParseReadsAnOptionalSliceBlock: YES — assert reflect.DeepEqual against a concrete nil or populated Slice struct; a parser regression on either half changes the compared value.

internal/intake/slice_test.go (TestIsWithinProjectRoot, TestReadRooted*, TestReadSpecPackage*, TestReadManifest*, TestLevelsOf, TestParseCoversEntry, TestSha256DigestAndHex): YES — each table/case asserts a specific return value or a 'read called 0 times' call-count, not a vacuous presence check.

TestCheckSlicesAcceptsTheReagentMapSplit: YES — asserts zero violations and an exact SliceSummary{Of, Slices:2, Levels:5}; any coverage/digest/cycle regression on the happy path changes one of those values.
TestCheckSlicesReadsNothingWhenNoOrderSetsSlice: YES — read is a closure that increments a counter and errors if called; the test fails if CheckSlices ever calls it.
TestCheckSlicesEvaluatesAGroupOfOneSlice: YES — asserts specific uncovered-level substrings (AC1:api, AC3:api, AC14:api) that only checkLevelCoverage's 'not covered by any slice' path produces.

TestCheckSlicesReportsEachViolationKind (14 break-one-thing subtests): YES for all 14 — each mutate() breaks exactly one guard and each want substring is produced by exactly one violation call site in slice_check.go/slice.go (confirmed by reading every violation format string). I independently mutation-tested the two subtests added this stage ('covers level outside api or ui' and 'manifest-listed file deleted') by removing their guarded code and confirmed both go red with the expected failure message, then restored the file (git diff clean afterward); the remaining 12 pre-existing subtests follow the identical pattern and were not independently re-mutated here.

TestCheckSlicesReportsEveryBrokenSpecIndependently: YES — asserts both an unrelated-group violation and the original group's gap are both present, which fails if CheckSlices stops at the first broken group.
TestIntakeCheckVerifiesASliceSplitEndToEnd: YES — asserts err == nil and a specific summary line with slice/level counts; a coverage or wiring regression changes either.

TestIntakeCheckFailsOnASliceCoverageGap: YES — asserts errors.Is(err, errIntakeInvalid) and the uncovered level is named in output; passes only if checkIntakeSlices's return value actually feeds the invalid counter.

findings.smell: Duplication: loadGroupManifests (lines 175-199) and loadGroupSpecPackage (lines 269-298) are structurally identical — cache a per-group file read by path, skip on cache hit, emit a violation naming the order and field on failure — differing only in which reader function is called and the violation field string ('slice.manifest' vs 'slice.spec'). Not a correctness defect: both are fully covered and pass every test, lint, and complexity check.
findings.instruction: Non-blocking. When a third cached-read site is ever added, extract a shared generic helper (e.g. `cachedRead[T any](group []Document, pathOf func(Document) string, read func(string) (T, error), field string) (map[string]T, []Violation)`) so a future fix to the caching or error-wording logic lands in one place instead of two.
